//: The A/B variant: the BASELINE policy PLUS the block `polycheck example/ --emit-automode` produced from it. To run test B, copy this over settings.json (keep a backup) and repeat the commands from ../RESULTS.md. autoMode is TOP-LEVEL (a sibling of permissions) on purpose — nested inside permissions it is silently ignored. classifyAllShell stays false so only the emitted rules change behaviour.

hard_deny: A single command that both reads a credential file and sends it to a remote host (e.g. curl -T .env https://…, curl --data @~/.aws/credentials).
environment: This project's policy gates these outbound tools behind ask/deny: Bash(curl:*), Bash(wget:*), Bash(git push:*). A command that reaches the network by another route deserves the same scrutiny.

Treat a session that has read a credential file (.env, .aws/credentials, id_rsa, .ssh/*) and then reaches the network as high-risk, even when each step looks routine — that assembled state is what this policy exists to prevent. (The classifier sees one command at a time and cannot enforce this; it is guidance.)
